scope.read_method: Official arXiv/GitHub/Hugging Face/Lichess pages plus bounded unauthenticated metadata and pinned documentation/source GETs. Only metadata projections, hashes and observations retained; no corpus rows saved.

revisions.equivalence: UNVERIFIED: no corpus bytes were read or compared; newer GitHub code/README cannot be silently treated as identical to the older HF release.

claims.claim: 50 tasks and 3,500 items: 1,100 structural, 600 motifs, 900 short tactics, 500 position judgment, 400 semantic.
Lichess puzzles/evaluations supply rule, motif, tactic and evaluation sources. Semantic originates in ChessBase 17 PGN comments with Qwen cleaning/relevance filtering and four distractor strategies.
Given FEN-before, a move and four comments, predict the source-associated comment letter; not free explanation generation or per-claim truth certification.
Current code shares 100 base state-move-comment triples across four variants and derives base_example_id from canonical four-field FEN, move and normalized comment.

HF expert-generated metadata does not establish that every released answer/explanation was independently expert-validated; paper-described relevance filtering is a different operation from factuality validation.
Code is MIT with notice obligations. Current README explicitly keeps benchmark data under source-material terms.
HF metadata says MIT and ships the same software-worded MIT file; current code README identifies purchased ChessBase17 commentary without an applicable commentary sublicense in the inspected sources.
Lichess database exports are CC0 and provider permits modification/redistribution. This does not license unrelated ChessBase comments.
Current semantic builder includes correct_text and fen_after in metadata and exports correct_answer separately. Whole-row model input would expose evaluator material.

No verified pretraining non-overlap or comparison to local source-game/board reservoirs was established. Treat repeated base examples, source games, canonical boards and comments as shared groups; never train on answer keys then claim independent performance.
